# Hypotheses
Here I am rewriting the hypothesis here for convinience.

H1: Attitudes toward gender equality differ significantly across gender groups.
  Categorical IV: Sex. Continuous DV: Gender equality composite. Composite items: Gender_Equality_1, Gender_Equality_2, Gender_Equality_3.

H2: Individuals reporting greater romantic intimacy with their partners report higher relationship satisfaction.
  Continuous IV: Romantic intimacy composite. Continuous DV: Relationship satisfaction. Composite IV items: Love_1 through Love_5. DV items: prqc_1 through prqc_3.

```{r load packages}

library(ggplot2)
```

# Load the processed data

```{r load data}
#these were the saved csv files from the dataprocessing rmd file.
h1Data <- read.csv("processed-data/H1.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("processed-data/H2.csv")
```

# Check the variable types to choose the plots

```{r check data}
str(h1Data)
str(h2Data)

# H1: Sex is categorical and avgGenderEq is continuous (boxplot, violin plot)
# H2: both variables are continuous -> scatterplot 

h1Data$Sex <- factor(h1Data$Sex,
                     levels = c("Men", "Women", "Non-binary", "Prefer not to say"))
table(h1Data$Sex)
```

# H1: Gender equality attitudes by sex

#H1: Boxplot

```{r h1 boxplot}
h1BoxPlot <- ggplot(data = h1Data,
                    aes(x = Sex,
                        y = avgGenderEq,
                        fill = Sex)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se,
               fun.args = list(mult = 1.96),
               geom = "errorbar",
               width = 0.2) +
  labs(x = "Sex",
       y = "Gender Equality Composite Score (1-7)",
       title = "Gender Equality Attitudes by Sex") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7) +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme_gray(base_size = 13)
h1BoxPlot
```

# H1: Violin plot (+ boxplot)

```{r h1 violin}
h1ViolinPlot <- ggplot(data = h1Data,
                       aes(x = Sex,
                           y = avgGenderEq,
                           fill = Sex)) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.08, fill = "white") +
  labs(x = "Sex",
       y = "Gender Equality Composite Score (1-7)",
       title = "Gender Equality Attitudes by Sex") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7) +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme_gray(base_size = 13)
h1ViolinPlot
```

# H2: Romantic intimacy and relationship satisfaction

# H2: Jittered scatterplot + regression

```{r h2 scatterplot}
# Scores are averages of a few items, so many people share the same value.
# geom_jitter() spreads the points slightly so overlapping points are visible (i.e., it adds noise.)

h2ScatterPlot <- ggplot(data = h2Data,
                        aes(x = avgLoveIntimacy,
                            y = avgPrqc)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.05,
              height = 0.05,
              alpha = 0.05,
              size = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Romantic Intimacy Composite Score (1-5)",
       y = "Relationship Satisfaction Composite Score (1-7)",
       title = "Romantic Intimacy and Relationship Satisfaction") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  theme_gray(base_size = 13)
h2ScatterPlot

# The plot shows an association only; it does not show that intimacy causes satisfaction!
```

# Saving figures

```{r save figures}
ggsave("plots/h1BoxPlot.pdf", plot = h1BoxPlot)
ggsave("plots/h1ViolinPlot.pdf", plot = h1ViolinPlot)
ggsave("plots/h2ScatterPlot.pdf", plot = h2ScatterPlot)
```
